items.title: $80K fine for dairy company based near Mississauga after worker hurt in fall
items.summary: A former longtime Mississauga company now located just over the border in Toronto has been fined $80,000 after one of its workers was injured in a fall last year. The Ontario Ministry of Labour said in a news release this week that Gay Lea Foods Co-operative Limited pleaded guilty in Provincial Offences Court in Guelph on Sept. 18 to an offence under the Occupational Health and Safety Act. Gay Lea Foods, Ontario’s largest farmer-owned dairy co-operative, has been located in Etobicoke near Toronto Pearson Airport since 2025 after basing its operations in Mississauga for nearly two decades. The incident occurred on March 23, 2025 at a Gay Lea Foods dairy processing plant in Guelph, west of the Greater Toronto Area, the ministry said. “A worker was injured after falling from the top of a milk transport truck while collecting milk samples. Gay Lea Foods Co-operative Limited failed, as an employer, to provide information, instruction and supervision to a worker with respect to the safe setup and operation of a hatch access system (gantry),” contrary to the Occupational Health and Safety Act, the ministry’s news release continued. According to the ministry, milk delivered to the Guelph plant is sampled by receivers before being unloaded. “Samples are collected from hatches located on top of milk transport trucks. Workers access the hatches using an elevated hatch access system, known as a gantry, which is equipped with steps and guardrails to help prevent falls,” the Ministry of Labour said. “To shorten the sampling process, some workers would step onto the top of the truck and walk to the second sampling hatch rather than repositioning the gantry. “On March 23, 2025, a milk receiver stepped from the gantry onto the top of a truck and was no longer protected by the guardrail system.

items.title: Home prices remain lower than a year ago in Mississauga
items.summary: The real estate market remained sluggish last month in Mississauga. Prices and sales were largely in line with August, although the average selling price saw a modest increase, real estate platform Zoocasa said in its analysis of the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. 5 per cent month-over-month to $929,600, Zoocasa said. But it is lower than September 2025 when the average was $969,501, according to Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. The Greater Toronto Area average selling price for the month was $1,006,409, down from $1,060,036 a year earlier. 2 per cent, with 1,371 properties coming onto the market in September, Zoocasa said. 8. Detached homes and condo apartments continued to see the most activity among Mississauga’s property types, Zoocasa noted. Detached home prices remained relatively flat, increasing less than one per cent to $1,285,467 month-over-month in Mississauga. The average price of a detached home in September 2025 was $1,380,811, according to TRREB data.

items.title: Meadowvale Metro Store to Close, Reopen as Food Basics Discount Grocer Next February
items.summary: According to Insauga, the Metro supermarket at Meadowvale Town Centre will close and reopen next year as a Food Basics discount grocery store. Metro spokesperson Stephanie Bonk told Insauga the location at 6677 Meadowvale Town Centre Circle will be converted to a Food Basics in February 2027, with the existing store remaining open until then. Bonk said the conversion itself is expected to take about three to four weeks. Food Basics is a discount banner owned by Metro Inc., which announced plans this summer to convert 10 of its Ontario supermarkets to the lower-price format, according to a Retail Insider report cited by Insauga. Metro confirmed this month that a Queen Street West location in Toronto is also being switched to Food Basics. Bonk said the shift reflects changing shopper habits, with customers increasingly looking for value-oriented grocery options. Insauga reports some Mississauga residents have welcomed news of a cheaper grocery option moving into the plaza.

items.title: Incumbent Jeff Clark Faces Challenger Mohanad Assal for Mississauga's Wards 9 and 10 Trustee Seat
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, incumbent trustee Jeff Clark faces challenger Mohanad Assal for the Wards 9 and 10 seat on the Peel District School Board in the Oct. 26 municipal election. Assal told the outlet he has volunteered with various election campaigns over the past several years, helping candidates running for city council and for federal office on election days. He said that experience gave him a better understanding of the election process, let him engage directly with residents, and taught him about the issues that matter most to the community. Mississauga.com reports Clark is seeking another term representing the two wards as part of its candidate profile series. The Wards 9 and 10 trustee race is one of several Peel board contests on Mississauga ballots this fall alongside the mayoral and city council races.

items.title: Mississauga: 65% Back Subway; Transit Priorities Split
items.summary: Sixty-five per cent support a subway extension, but residents split 45% to 44% on subway versus all-day, two-way Milton GO service. Confidence combines very and somewhat confident. October 7, 2026 (Toronto, ON) - A new Liaison Strategies Mississauga survey finds 65% of residents support extending subway service to downtown Mississauga near Square One. Asked which would be the better transit investment, 45% choose the subway extension and 44% choose all-day, two-way GO service on the Milton line. The findings follow Bonnie Crombie's September 24 proposal to extend Toronto's Line 2 into Mississauga. Liaison surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from October 2 to October 4, 2026, using Interactive Voice Recording (IVR) technology. Participants were reached through random digit dialling (RDD) across both landline and cellular phone networks. items.title: Crombie Says Police Are Investigating Social Media Threats as Candidates Point to Toxic Online Discourse
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Peel Regional Police are investigating threats mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie says she received on social media, after she filed a complaint against Ward 5 council candidate Danny Singh. Singh denies any wrongdoing and told the Star he is not aware of a police investigation into him. The Star reports Singh's public social media posts have also troubled his opponent in the Ward 5 race, Councillor Natalie Hart, who sent him two cease-and-desist letters last year. Singh, a former executive assistant to Mayor Carolyn Parrish, suggested instead that the investigation shows Crombie interfering in his campaign. The complaint comes amid broader concern about toxic political discourse this election, which the Star says has included a volunteer for mayoral candidate Alvin Tedjo's campaign being attacked with a knife while installing signs on Monday night. The Star notes similar tension has surfaced in Orangeville, where a former councillor and deputy mayor running for mayor has faced related concerns. Hart won a 2024 byelection for the Ward 5 seat left vacant when Parrish moved up to mayor following Crombie's departure to run for the federal Liberal leadership.

items.title: Poll Finds Mississauga Voters Back a Subway Extension but Doubt It Will Ever Happen
items.summary: According to a new poll from Liaison Strategies, 65 per cent of Mississauga voters support extending the TTC's Line 2 subway from Kipling Station into the city, an idea mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie has championed, while 20 per cent are opposed. Crombie has proposed extending the Bloor-Danforth line from Kipling to Sherway Gardens and into downtown Mississauga, possibly with a stop near the new Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital. Despite the support, the poll found residents are skeptical it will actually happen, with 35 per cent saying they are not at all confident and another 26 per cent not very confident. Voters were split on whether the subway extension or two-way all-day GO service on the Milton line matters more, with 45 per cent backing the subway and 44 per cent backing GO service, a divide that tracked closely with support for Crombie versus incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish. Liaison Strategies principal David Valentin said the subway idea draws majority support across the main candidate groups, showing its appeal reaches beyond the candidate promoting it. The poll found slightly more optimism about the GO service plan, pointing to recent support voiced by Prime Minister Mark Carney and Premier Doug Ford, though neither has committed to a timeline.

items.title: Retail theft increasingly 'sophisticated' and now work of organized crime, experts say
items.summary: Retail theft has evolved from individual shoplifting into a crime increasingly committed by organized criminal networks, according to Peel Regional Police.

items.title: Mississauga and Brampton Houses of Worship to See More Police on Oct. 7 Anniversary
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police say officers will be visible at Muslim and Jewish places of worship in Mississauga and Brampton on Tuesday, the anniversary of the Oct. 7, 2023 attack in Israel. Police said in a release that they are aware of planned demonstrations and want everyone in the community to be able to gather, worship and demonstrate safely and peacefully. Insauga reports the 2023 attack involved coordinated armed incursions from Gaza into southern Israel during the Jewish holiday of Simchat Torah, killing more than 1,000 people including 36 children, with more than 360 civilians killed at the Nova music festival and over 250 taken hostage. Israel's military operation in Gaza has continued since. Peel police asked anyone attending demonstrations or community gatherings to remain peaceful and let others worship without fear or intimidation. The force said a similar announcement came from Durham Regional Police, which increased patrols near Jewish places of worship during Yom Kippur after antisemitic threats were made. Peel police said it takes any hate-motivated threats or actions against community members seriously and will respond accordingly.

items.title: Wasaga Beach Man Facing Drug Charges Also Accused in 2023 Mississauga Shooting Death
items.summary: According to CTV News, Shammar Osbourne, a 22-year-old from Wasaga Beach, appeared in a Collingwood courtroom Tuesday facing drug possession and trafficking charges while separately accused of first-degree murder in a 2023 Mississauga shooting. Peel Regional Police allege Osbourne was one of four people, including a woman and three men, charged in June in connection with the March 2023 shooting death of 29-year-old Bryan Lara-Alvarez outside a Mississauga home. Investigators said Lara-Alvarez was found with gunshot wounds and died from his injuries, and that an SUV was seen fleeing the scene. CTV News reports police also charged 22-year-old Shamba Tull of Toronto with murder, while two other co-accused face firearms charges, and that search and arrest warrants led to a seized gun. Osbourne is scheduled to appear in virtual courtrooms in Barrie and Brampton next week, and CTV News notes the allegations against him have not been tested in court.

items.title: 74% of Mississauga Voters Want Personal Insults Out of the Mayoral Race, Poll Finds
items.summary: According to Insauga, a new poll from Liaison Strategies found 74 per cent of Mississauga voters say personal insults have no place in the mayoral campaign or anywhere else in the election. The survey was conducted immediately after last Thursday's debate, the second this election season to feature the four highest-profile mayoral candidates, during which Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie traded a number of heated exchanges. Just 14 per cent of respondents described the 2026 campaign as mostly respectful. Insauga reports Parrish and Crombie have also exchanged jabs and attacks on social media throughout the race, while city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, also among the 14 mayoral candidates, have taken each other and the two frontrunners to task on various issues in earlier debates. Liaison Strategies said it surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from Oct. 2 to 4 using interactive voice recording technology, reaching participants through random digit dialing across landlines and cellphones. Voters go to the polls on Oct. 26, though Insauga notes many may choose to cast ballots during advance voting, which began Tuesday.

items.title: Port Credit's Fall'N The Port Festival Brings Alpacas, Scarecrow Hunt and a Shot at Riding a 'Unicorn'
items.summary: According to Insauga, the Fall'N The Port festival takes over Brant Avenue in Port Credit later this month with farm animals, crafts and live entertainment for families. Insauga reports one of the event's biggest draws will be a petting area with alpacas, goats, rabbits and a donkey, alongside face painting and busking performers. Organizers are also hiding 30 scarecrows across participating Port Credit businesses for a neighbourhood-wide hunt, with maps available at the BIA tent. Families who find and identify all 30 scarecrows can enter a draw for a family prize pack. Insauga reports the grand prize gives one winner the chance to ride a unicorn, or at least a convincing stand-in for one.
